}}'''Daniel Wayne Armstrong''' is an American chemist who specializes in separation science, chiral molecular recognition, bioanalytic analysis, mass spectrometry and colloid chemistry. He is the Robert A. Welch Distinguished Professor at the [[University of Texas at Arlington]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Armstrong|first=Daniel|date=|title=UT Arlington profile|url=https://www.uta.edu/profiles/daniel-armstrong|url-status=live|website=www.uta.edu|publisher=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161112160912/https://www.uta.edu/profiles/daniel-armstrong |archive-date=2016-11-12 }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Daniel Armstrong - American Chemical Society|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/other/public/daniel-armstrong-biography-1998.html|url-status=live|access-date=|website=American Chemical Society|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150130154250/http://www.acs.org:80/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/other/public/daniel-armstrong-biography-1998.html |archive-date=2015-01-30 }}</ref> He has authored ~ 750 publications including 35 book chapters, a book, and holds over 35 patents on separation technologies.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Armstrong DW|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=c6FJgJ4AAAAJ&hl=en&oi=ao|access-date=2021-02-25|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Daniel W. Armstrong|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Daniel_Armstrong|url-status=live|access-date=|website=ResearchGate|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161112144727/https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Daniel_Armstrong |archive-date=2016-11-12 }}</ref> He was an associate editor for the prestigious [[American Chemical Society]] journal [[Analytical Chemistry (journal)|Analytical Chemistry]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Editors American Chemical Society|url=http://pubs.acs.org/page/ancham/editors.html|url-status=live|access-date=|website=pubs.acs.org|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160517013222/http://pubs.acs.org/page/ancham/editors.html |archive-date=2016-05-17 }}</ref> He is a fellow of the American Chemical Society, Royal Chemical Society (UK), and the [[National Academy of Inventors]]. Armstrong has given over 560 invited seminars worldwide at international conferences, universities and corporations.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Daniel W. Armstrong to Receive ACS Award in Separation Science and Technology 2014|url=http://www.chromatographyonline.com/daniel-w-armstrong-receive-acs-award-separation-science-and-technology-2014|url-status=live|access-date=|website=www.chromatographyonline.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161112143110/http://www.chromatographyonline.com/daniel-w-armstrong-receive-acs-award-separation-science-and-technology-2014 |archive-date=2016-11-12 }}</ref> His research and patents formed the basis for two companies: Advanced Separation Technologies, Inc; which was acquires by Sigma-Aldrich Corporation in 2006<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biospace.com/sigma-aldrich-corporation-acquires-b-advanced-separation-technologies-inc-b|title=Sigma-Aldrich Corporation Acquires Advanced Separation Technologies Inc.|website=BioSpace|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-09}}</ref> and AZYP, LLC in Arlington, TX.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.azypusa.com/|title=AZYP, LLC – Separations & Analytics|language=en-US|access-date=2019-11-09}}</ref>  His published work has been cited over 50,000 times and his h-index is 115.<ref name=":2" /> He is believed to have mentored more graduate level analytical chemists than any living scientist.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://academictree.org/chemistry/tree.php?pid=93392|title=Chemistry Tree - Daniel W. Armstrong Family Tree|website=academictree.org|access-date=2019-11-09}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Daniel W. Armstrong was born in 1949 to Robert E. Armstrong, an educator and mayor of Fort Wayne, IN and Nila L. Armstrong. He was the oldest of their three sons. As an undergraduate student, he played collegiate football and track & field.  He is married to Linda M. Armstrong and they have three children.

== Early career ==
Armstrong received his B.S. from [[Washington and Lee University]]. He received M.S. in oceanography and Ph.D. in bio-organic chemistry from [[Texas A&M University]]. Armstrong began his career at [[Bowdoin College]] as an assistant professor in 1978 and moved to [[Georgetown University]] in 1980, followed by [[Texas Tech University]] and then the [[Missouri University of Science and Technology|University of Missouri Rolla]] as a curator's distinguished professor. Later he joined [[Iowa State University]] in 2000 as the first Caldwell Distinguished Professor. He joined [[University of Texas at Arlington]] in 2006 as the Robert A. Welch Distinguished Professor, where he currently leads a research group in diverse areas of chiral molecular recognitions, ionic liquids, separation mechanism and theory, ultra-fast analysis, D-amino acid and peptide analysis and gas and liquid chromatography instrumentation and detectors.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />
